title: Magnitude, unit vector, direction angle
problem: For $\mathbf{v} = (-4, 3)$, find (a) the magnitude, (b) the unit vector, and (c) the angle $\mathbf{v}$ makes with the positive $x$-axis.

steps.instruction: Find the unit vector by dividing $\mathbf{v}$ by its magnitude.
Determine the direction angle, checking the quadrant first ($x < 0$, $y > 0$ places $\mathbf{v}$ in the second quadrant).

title: Vector arithmetic
problem: Given $\mathbf{a} = 3\mathbf{i} - \mathbf{j}$ and $\mathbf{b} = -\mathbf{i} + 4\mathbf{j}$, find $2\mathbf{a} - 3\mathbf{b}$ and its magnitude.

steps.instruction: Find the magnitude of the result.

title: Magnitude-direction form to components
problem: A boat is travelling at 12 km/h on a bearing of 060° (measured clockwise from north). Express the velocity as a component vector in the form $a\mathbf{i} + b\mathbf{j}$, where $\mathbf{i}$ is east and $\mathbf{j}$ is north.

steps.instruction: Recall that for a bearing of $B°$ (clockwise from north), the east-component is $|\mathbf{v}|\sin B°$ and the north-component is $|\mathbf{v}|\cos B°$ — the opposite of standard angle conventions.
